header.userPrompt:
Improve the bank-statement review page (web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala) with five related fixes. The page shows one bank statement's rows across the Ready / Unprocessed / Ignored / Linked / All tabs, with per-row actions and a bulk bar. Keep every existing behavior except where a fix explicitly changes it. Do NOT touch the draft->confirm flow, the AiSuggestions model/column, the JEV or Nova suggestions engines, the regenerate endpoint, or the auto-reconcile page.

FIX 1 — Show the full (multi-line) row description (web only).
The Description cell clamps text to one line (maxWidth 280px, overflow hidden, textOverflow ellipsis, whiteSpace nowrap), so long/multi-line descriptions are cut off with no way to read them. Wrap the description Typography in an MUI Tooltip whose title is the full `row.description`, so hovering reveals the complete text. KEEP the clamped single-line display in the table cell (do NOT change it to wrap — that would blow up row height across the table). Only attach the tooltip when the description is non-empty. The txnType chip below the description stays as-is.

FIX 2 — Make the page responsive (fix the lag) (web only).
The page is a single ~1000-line monolithic FunctionalComponent. Today ANY state change — opening/closing the "…" menu, toggling one checkbox, showing the toast, and the 3-second AI-suggestions poll that refetches the whole statement — re-renders the ENTIRE tree, including all rows (statements can have 80+ rows, each with several MUI Chips/Buttons/IconButtons). On top of that, each render recomputes the rule verdict and resolveImport ~4-5x PER ROW (ruleVerdictFor, resolveImport, isReadyToProcess are each called from filteredRows, the counts, rowPrimaryAction, matchCell, categoryCell). That is the source of the perceived slowness and the lag when opening/closing the "…" menu.

Success criterion: opening or closing the "…" menu, and toggling a single row's checkbox, must NOT recompute rule verdicts for every row and must NOT re-render every other row's MUI subtree. Concrete levers (apply all that are needed to meet the criterion):
  a) Precompute per-row data ONCE per render in the parent: a Map keyed by row id holding the rule verdict and the ResolvedImport (and derived isReady). Have filteredRows, the tab counts, and the cells read from this map instead of recomputing. This removes the O(rows x rules x 5) work per render.
  b) Extract the table row into its own child component that receives already-computed values as props (the row, its precomputed verdict + ResolvedImport + isReady flag, selected flag, the category/merchant display values, and stable callbacks). Memoize it so unchanged rows are skipped on re-render — follow any existing memoization pattern in the web module; if slinky offers no memo helper, at minimum structure props so the row is cheap and isolate the menu/overlay state (below) so a menu open/close does not live in a scope that rebuilds the table.
  c) Replace the hand-rolled fixed-position "…" dropdown (the `menuAnchorPos`/`menuForRow` custom Box overlay) with an MUI Menu/Popover anchored to the IconButton. The current custom menu has NO Esc handler and no focus management; MUI Menu provides Esc-to-close and focus handling natively. Preserve the same actions (as revised by Fix 3).
Respect the frontend gotchas in CLAUDE.md's self-check: object-level `val`s must hold only plain JS literals (no ReactElement/KeyAddingStage); use `def` for React elements reused in a tree; use the `(opt: Any) match` pattern (never js.Dynamic) in MUI callbacks. The route is unchanged and the page stays reachable.

FIX 3 — Make the "…" menu state-aware, and show the real category/merchant on Linked rows.
3a (web only): The overflow menu today always offers "Link to existing expense" / "Create import rule" / "Ignore" regardless of row state, so a row that already created an expense is still offered Link and Ignore. Make the menu items depend on the row's state:
  - Linked (expenseId or refundId set): show "Unlink" only — call the EXISTING handleUnlink (expense) or handleUnlinkRefund (refund). Do not show Link/Ignore.
  - Ignored (ignoredAt set): show "Un-ignore" only — call the EXISTING handleUnignore.
  - Otherwise (unprocessed/ready): keep "Link to existing expense" / "Create import rule" / "Ignore" as today.
  Prefer expressing "which menu items for this row state" as a small PURE function on the page object so it is unit-testable.
3b (backend + web): In the Linked tab the Category column shows "—" because the row model carries no category for the linked expense. Surface it:
  - Add two optional fields to GetBankStatement.StatementRowData (lib/api/shared/.../bankstatements/GetBankStatement.scala): the linked expense's category id and merchant id (follow existing naming, e.g. expenseCategoryId / expenseMerchantId). Update its Json format + Schema accordingly.
  - Populate them in GetBankStatementAction / BankStatementRepository for rows whose expense_id is set, from the linked expense: its merchant id, and its category. An expense can have MULTIPLE category splits — surface the category id ONLY when the expense has exactly ONE split; when it has multiple splits leave it None (do NOT guess a primary). The query MUST be user-scoped (WHERE user_id = ?) with a stable ORDER BY. Reuse the existing expense/splits repository entities and the same join shape used by the AI-suggestions history-tier query (expense_id -> expense -> single category split); do not duplicate query logic or invent a second path.
  - Web: in categoryCell, for a linked row show the real category name (map the new category id against categoryList) instead of the dash; when it is None for a linked row (multi-split or missing) show "Multiple" (or a dash) rather than guessing. In matchCell, for a linked row show the merchant name from the new merchant id when present, otherwise keep the "Linked" chip. Non-linked rows keep their current rule/AI display and "AI" tag unchanged.

FIX 4 — Ready-tab "Confirm" should open the prefilled drawer for review, not import immediately (web only).
Today the per-row primary action on a Ready row (the "Confirm" / "Import refund" button) calls handleBulkImport directly and creates the expense with no chance to override the AI/rule merchant or category. Change it: for a ready, NON-Ignore row the per-row primary button should OPEN the existing drawer prefilled with the resolved suggestion — for a negative-amount row open BankRowCreateExpenseForm (setCreatingForRow), for a positive-amount row the refund form — so the user can adjust merchant/category before submitting. Reuse the EXISTING drawer and form: BankRowCreateExpenseForm.initialSelection already prefills rule-winner-first then AI suggestion, so no new prefill logic is needed — just route the button to open the drawer instead of importing. For a ready row whose rule verdict is Ignore, keep the one-click "Ignore" button exactly as-is. KEEP the bulk "Process ready" bar as the fast one-click path (it still imports directly via handleBulkImport, unchanged). Net result: single-row Confirm = review-in-drawer; bulk bar = fast path.

CONSTRAINTS (all fixes):
- Follow docs/guide (antipatterns, backend, frontend, data-infra, testing, ci-checklist) and CLAUDE.md.
- Surgical: every changed line traces to one of these five fixes. Do not restyle or refactor unrelated code, comments, or formatting beyond what Fix 2 requires. Do not change dependencies (build.sbt, plugins.sbt, build.properties, package.json); revert any incidental yarn.lock churn from a local build (the dependencies reviewer enforces this).
- Backend: user-scoped DB access (WHERE user_id = ?) on the new/changed query; stable ORDER BY; no DB CHECK constraints; fail loud on missing data (no silent defaults); use Chimney for case-class mapping; prefer enums over stringly-typed values; never drop a Future; log any new user-scoped operation with the userId in scope AFTER the user is resolved (coding-patterns reviewer).
- Prefer extracting small PURE functions on the page object (menu items for a row state; the linked-row category/merchant display decision) so they are unit-testable, mirroring how resolveImport is already structured.
- Tests:
  - web: keep the existing BankStatementReviewPageSpec passing (resultLabel, suggestionsPending, canRegenerateSuggestions, resolveImport). Add tests for the state-aware menu function (3a), the linked-row category/merchant display helper (3b), and the Ready-row Confirm-opens-drawer behavior (4). Component tests must use BrowserRouter + jsdom; `null.asInstanceOf[API]` only when the component never calls ctx.api.
  - server: add a repository test for the new linked-expense lookup — user-scoped (ignores other users), surfaces the merchant id, surfaces the category id only for a single-split expense and None for a multi-split expense.
  - Verify per-task with targeted `sbt "testOnly *Spec"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`; the final stage runs the full suite. web/test needs Node 24 with NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider.
- Attribution: do NOT include any Claude session links (claude.ai/ or a Claude-Session footer) in commit messages or the PR description. `Co-Authored-By: Claude` IS allowed.

resultJson.description:
Five related fixes to the bank-statement review page (`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala`), which shows one statement's rows across the Ready / Unprocessed / Ignored / Linked / All tabs.

1. Hovering a clamped description shows the full text in a tooltip.
2. The page stops lagging. Today every state change re-renders every row and re-runs the rule verdict and resolveImport about 5 times per row. The fix computes per-row data once, moves each row into its own memoized component, and replaces the hand-rolled "…" overlay with an MUI Menu, which also gives Esc-to-close and focus handling.
3. The "…" menu depends on the row's state: Linked rows get Unlink, Ignored rows get Un-ignore, all other rows keep Link / Create rule / Ignore. Linked rows show the real category and merchant of the linked expense. This needs two new optional fields on `GetBankStatement.StatementRowData`, filled by a new user-scoped query. The category only appears when the expense has exactly one split.
4. The per-row "Confirm" / "Import refund" button on a Ready row opens the existing prefilled drawer, so the user can review merchant and category first. The bulk "Process ready" bar stays as the fast one-click import.

Every changed line must trace to one of these fixes. Do not touch: the draft→confirm flow, the AiSuggestions model, the JEV/Nova engines, the regenerate endpoint, the auto-reconcile page, or any dependency/build files. Revert any yarn.lock churn. Decision logic goes into small pure functions on the `BankStatementReviewPage` object (the same way `resolveImport` is built) so it gets plain unit tests, not DOM tests.

tasks.title: Backend: surface the linked expense's merchant id and single-split category id on statement rows (Fix 3b, API + server)
tasks.description:
1. In lib/api/shared/.../bankstatements/GetBankStatement.scala, add `expenseMerchantId: Option[UUID]` and `expenseCategoryId: Option[UUID]` to `StatementRowData`. Json.format and Schema.derived pick them up automatically; no defaults. Fix every constructor call in test fixtures: web/src/test/.../pages/BankStatementReviewPageSpec.scala (sampleRow), web/src/test/.../pages/BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec.scala (row) and web/src/test/.../utils/ReconciliationMatcherSpec.scala (makeRow). Set both new fields to None there.
2. Add a small repository model in server/.../repositories/models/, e.g. `BankStatementRowLinkedExpense(rowId: UUID, merchantId: Option[UUID], categoryId: Option[UUID])`.
3. Add a DAO method to BankStatementRowDAO, e.g. `linkedExpenses(bankStatementId: UUID, userId: UUID)(implicit conn): List[BankStatementRowLinkedExpense]`. Mirror the single-split join shape in `categoryHistory`:
   - FROM bank_statement_row bsr
   - JOIN bank_statement bs ON bs.id = bsr.bank_statement_id AND bs.user_id = userId
   - JOIN expense e ON e.id = bsr.expense_id AND e.user_id = userId
   - LEFT JOIN (SELECT expense_id FROM expense_category_split WHERE user_id = userId GROUP BY expense_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 1) single_split ON single_split.expense_id = bsr.expense_id
   - LEFT JOIN expense_category_split ecs ON ecs.expense_id = single_split.expense_id AND ecs.user_id = userId
   - WHERE bsr.bank_statement_id = bankStatementId
   - ORDER BY bsr.index, bsr.id
   - SELECT bsr.id, e.merchant_id, ecs.category_id
   Multi-split and zero-split expenses come back with category None.
4. Add a repository method `findRowLinkedExpenses(bankStatementId, userId): Future[List[...]]` on BankStatementRepository (Future { withConnection }).
5. In GetBankStatementAction, add the call to the for-comprehension after the statement view is resolved. Build a Map by rowId. Replace the manual StatementRowData construction with Chimney: `r.into[GetBankStatement.StatementRowData].withFieldComputed(_.expenseMerchantId, ...).withFieldComputed(_.expenseCategoryId, ...).transform`. Add a logger.info with userId and statement id after the view is resolved (coding-patterns reviewer rule).
6. Tests in BankStatementRepositorySpec, a new "findRowLinkedExpenses" block, using RepositoryUtils plus the existing private helpers (createCategorizedExpense/createRows; extend createCategorizedExpense to accept a merchantId if needed):
   - surfaces the merchant id and the category id for a single-split expense
   - category is None for a multi-split expense, but the merchant id is still there
   - unlinked rows are absent
   - another user's data is never returned (pass userB's id for userA's statement → empty)
7. Verify: `CI=true sbt Test/compile`, then `sbt "server/testOnly *BankStatementRepositorySpec"`. If a controller spec covers GET bank statement, run it too (`sbt "server/testOnly *BankStatementsControllerSpec"`).

tasks.title: Web: full-description tooltip and Ready-row Confirm opens the prefilled drawer (Fix 1 + Fix 4)
tasks.description:
Fix 1: in the Description cell, wrap the existing clamped description Typography in an MUI Tooltip whose title is `row.description`. Only wrap when `row.description.nonEmpty`. Keep the clamp styling (maxWidth 280px, nowrap, ellipsis) and the txnType chip exactly as they are.

Fix 4: add a pure function to the page object, e.g. `primaryActionFor(row, isReady: Boolean, verdict: RowRuleVerdict.Verdict): PrimaryAction`, with a small ADT/enum. Cases: Linked (disabled), Unignore, IgnoreByRule (the one-click Ignore, unchanged), ReviewExpense (ready, non-Ignore, amount < 0), ReviewRefund (ready, non-Ignore, amount > 0), CreateRefund, CreateExpense. Make `rowPrimaryAction` render from it:
- ReviewExpense: keeps the "Confirm" label and contained style, but onClick does `setCreatingForRow(Some(row.id)); setLinkingForRow(None)`. Do NOT call handleBulkImport.
- ReviewRefund: keeps the "Import refund" label, onClick does `setCreatingRefundForRow(Some(row.id))`.
- Everything else behaves exactly as today.
The bulk "Process ready" bar keeps calling handleBulkImport unchanged. No new prefill logic: BankRowCreateExpenseForm.initialSelection already prefills rule first, then AI.

Tests in BankStatementReviewPageSpec: new `"primaryActionFor" should {...}` block (method name only as the subject). Cover:
- a ready negative row with a SetMerchant/NoRule verdict → ReviewExpense
- a ready positive row → ReviewRefund
- a ready row with an Ignore verdict → IgnoreByRule
- linked → Linked
- ignored → Unignore
- not-ready negative → CreateExpense; not-ready positive → CreateRefund

Verify: `CI=true sbt Test/compile`, then `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewPageSpec"`.

tasks.title: Web: make the review page responsive (Fix 2: precompute per-row data, memoized row component, MUI Menu)
tasks.description:
Goal: opening/closing the "…" menu or toggling one checkbox must not recompute rule verdicts for every row and must not re-render other rows' MUI subtrees.

(a) Precompute in the parent with `Hooks.useMemo(() => ..., List(statementRows, ruleList, merchantList, statement.flatMap(_.aiSuggestions), categoryList))`. Use List deps, never js.Array, for new hooks (frontend.md RULE-FE-006). Produce a `Map[UUID, RowInfo]` with: verdict (RowRuleVerdict.verdict once per row), `resolved: Option[ResolvedImport]` (call the existing pure `BankStatementReviewPage.resolveImport`; it recomputes the verdict internally, which is acceptable, or add an overload taking a precomputed verdict without changing the existing signature or tests), `isReady`, and the display strings the cells need (category name, merchant name, categoryFromAi). Make filteredRows, the four tab counts, handleBulkImport's Ignore check, and the cells read from this map. Remove the now-unused inner `ruleVerdictFor`, `resolveImport` and `isReadyToProcess` defs if nothing uses them any more.

(b) Extract the table row into a child component in the same page object (or a new `BankStatementReviewRow` object in the pages package), following RULE-FE-001 (case class Props, `val component: FunctionalComponent[Props]`, `def apply` returning KeyAddingStage). Props:
- the row, its RowInfo, selected and showCheckbox flags, pollingSuggestions
- stable callbacks: `onToggleSelected(rowId, checked)` and `onAction(rowId, action)`
Memoize it. Slinky 0.7.5 has no existing memo usage in this repo; check that `slinky.core.facade.React.memo(component, (a, b) => a == b)` compiles. Slinky wraps Scala props in one JS object, so React's default shallow compare would always fail; an explicit `==` comparator on the case class is required. Callbacks must keep the same reference between renders, otherwise `==` fails. Wrap them with `Hooks.useCallback(..., List(stmtId))` (or ""). They may only use setters with functional updates and stable values; after the previous task, row actions no longer call handleBulkImport. Move tintChip/dash/suggestingOrDash/matchCell/categoryCell/rowPrimaryAction rendering into the row component. Element helpers stay `def`s inside the render, never object-level vals (RULE-FE-002/003). Keep `.withKey(row.id.toString)` on each row.

(c) Delete the custom fixed-position overlay and the `menuAnchorPos`/`menuForRow` state. Each row owns its "…" IconButton plus an `mui.Menu` with local `anchorEl` state (useState of an optional dom.Element). Opening or closing it then re-renders only that row. Use MenuItems for the same three actions as today (Link to existing expense → set linkingForRow and clear creatingForRow; Create import rule → ruleFormForRow; Ignore → handleIgnore), each closing the menu. Get the anchor from the click event's currentTarget. If a cast is needed, add a typed helper to `MuiCompat` with a test in MuiCompatSpec, because js.Dynamic/asInstanceOf are banned in pages (RULE-FE-014). Use the `(opt: Any) match` pattern in any MUI callback that hands back js.Any. Keep the Fix 1 tooltip and Fix 4 primary-action behaviour intact.

Tests:
- the existing BankStatementReviewPageSpec must still pass
- add a unit test for any new pure precompute helper, e.g. `rowInfo(...)`: ready flag for an Ignore-rule row, ready flag for a row with a resolved import, display names
- optional: a render-without-crash jsdom test for the row component (BrowserRouter, `null.asInstanceOf[API]` only if it never calls ctx.api), guarding the Slinky element-reuse risk introduced by the extraction, with a comment saying that is the reason (RULE-TE-010)
Verify: `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewPageSpec"`.

tasks.title: Web: state-aware "…" menu and real category/merchant on Linked rows (Fix 3a + Fix 3b web)
tasks.description:
3a: add a pure function on the page object, e.g. `menuItemsFor(row: GetBankStatement.StatementRowData): List[RowMenuItem]`, with an ADT/enum `RowMenuItem = LinkExpense | CreateRule | Ignore | Unlink | UnlinkRefund | Unignore`. Precedence:
- expenseId set → List(Unlink)
- else refundId set → List(UnlinkRefund)
- else ignoredAt set → List(Unignore)
- else List(LinkExpense, CreateRule, Ignore)
Render the row's MUI Menu from this list. Unlink → existing `handleUnlink(stmt.id, rowId)`; UnlinkRefund → existing `handleUnlinkRefund`; Unignore → existing `handleUnignore`. All three appear as "Unlink" / "Un-ignore". The other items behave as today. Route them through the row's stable `onAction` callback.

3b web: add a pure helper on the page object for the linked-row display, e.g. `linkedCategoryDisplay(row, categories): LinkedCategory` (Named(name) | Multiple | Unknown) and `linkedMerchantName(row, merchants): Option[String]`. Rules:
- Expense-linked row with `expenseCategoryId = Some(id)` found in categoryList → the name. With None → Multiple, rendered as a "Multiple" chip. The id isn't stored, so multi-split and missing can't be told apart, and we must not guess a category.
- Id not found (lists still loading), or a refund-only link → dash.
- Merchant: name from `expenseMerchantId` when it resolves in merchantList; otherwise keep the "Linked" chip.
Use these in categoryCell and matchCell for linked rows only, or precompute them into the per-row display data if the previous task introduced it. Non-linked rows keep their current rule/AI display and the "AI" tag unchanged.

Tests in BankStatementReviewPageSpec (subjects are method names only):
- `menuItemsFor`: linked expense, linked refund, ignored, unprocessed, ready
- `linkedCategoryDisplay`: single category resolves to its name, None → Multiple, unknown id → Unknown, refund-only → Unknown/dash
- `linkedMerchantName`: present → name, absent/unknown → None
Verify: `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewPageSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- lib/api/shared: Tapir endpoints and request/response models shared by server and web. The model to change is lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/bankstatements/GetBankStatement.scala. `StatementRowData(id, index, date: LocalDate, amount: BigDecimal, description, manuallyEdited, confirmedAt: Option[Instant], expenseId: Option[UUID], refundId: Option[UUID], ignoredAt: Option[Instant], txnType: String)` uses `Json.format` and `Schema.derived...name(SName("BankStatementRowData"))`. There are no default params; adding fields breaks constructor calls only in 3 web test fixtures: BankStatementReviewPageSpec.sampleRow, BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec.row, utils/ReconciliationMatcherSpec.makeRow. Server constructs it only in GetBankStatementAction. GetDocument.StatementRowData is a DIFFERENT class; leave it alone.
- lib/api/shared/.../api/utils/RowRuleVerdict.scala: `sealed trait Verdict; NoRule; Ignore; SetMerchant(merchantId: Option[UUID])`, `verdict(rules: List[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule], description): Verdict` and `ruleMerchantId(rules, description): Option[UUID]`. Both call ImportRuleMatcher.findRowWinner, so this is the expensive call per row.
- server: controllers → actions → repositories → DAOs (Anorm).
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/GetBankStatementAction.scala: `apply(id, userId): Future[GetBankStatement.Response]`. It does `bankStatementRepository.find(id, userId)` (throws "Bank statement not found" when the result is None), then `findRows(id)`, then maps rows by hand. No logger today. The controller (server/src/main/scala/controllers/BankStatementsController.scala `getOne`) doesn't log either.
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepository.scala: every method is `Future { database.withConnection/withTransaction { implicit conn => DAO... } }` on DatabaseExecutionContext. Never compose futures in a repository.
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/BankStatementRowDAO.scala: has `categoryHistory(userId)`, the AI-suggestions history-tier query whose single-split join shape (bank_statement_row → bank_statement scoped by user_id → expense_category_split scoped by user_id → `(SELECT expense_id FROM expense_category_split WHERE user_id=? GROUP BY expense_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 1) single_split`) the new query must mirror. Columns: bank_statement_row(id, bank_statement_id, index, date, amount, description, …, expense_id, refund_id, ignored_at, txn_type); expense(id, user_id, amount, date, time, merchant_id, notes, …); expense_category_split(id, user_id, expense_id, category_id, amount). Postgres 13 in tests has no MIN(uuid), so use the join shape and avoid aggregates on uuid. UUID params are written as `${x.toString}::UUID`.
  - Repository models: server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/models/ (BankStatementRow has extra bankStatementId/createdAt/updatedAt fields; Expense; ExpenseCategorySplit).
  - Chimney is already used (`import io.scalaland.chimney.dsl.*`, e.g. ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction `transformInto`). BankStatementRow → StatementRowData via `.into[...].withFieldComputed(...).transform` works; extra source fields are ignored.
- server tests: server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepositorySpec.scala extends RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils and uses `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }` and `.futureValue`. It already has private helpers `createCategorizedExpense(userId, categoryIds*)` (merchantId hardcoded None; add a param if needed), `createRows(userId, descriptions)` and `link(row, userId, categoryId)`, and calls `repositories.bankStatements.setRowExpenseIdForUser(rowId, userId, expenseId, now)`. RepositoryUtils (server/src/test/scala/utils/RepositoryUtils.scala) provides createUser(email=Email.trusted(..)), createCategory(userId, name), createMerchant(userId, name, notes, categoryId) and createExpense(userId, ..., merchantId, splits). Use these; never seed with raw SQL. Two-user tests use `createUser(email = net.wiringbits.common.models.Email.trusted("a@test.com"))`.
- web: Scala.js + Slinky 0.7.5 + React 18 + MUI 5 (ScalablyTyped, `import com.olvind.mui.muiMaterial.components as mui`).
  - The page: web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala (~990 lines, one FunctionalComponent). Object-level pure fns: statementMetadataLine, resultLabel, suggestionsPending, canRegenerateSuggestions, `final case class ResolvedImport(merchantId: Option[UUID], categoryId: UUID, categoryFromAi: Boolean)`, and `resolveImport(ruleList, merchants, aiSuggestions: Option[AiSuggestions], row): Option[ResolvedImport]` (None for Ignore-verdict rows or when nothing resolves; AI only used when status Done).
  - Inside the component: ruleVerdictFor/resolveImport/isReadyToProcess (ready = no expense, no refund, not ignored, amount < 0, and (verdict Ignore or resolveImport defined)). Because amount < 0 is required, positive rows are never Ready today, so the "Import refund" branch is effectively unreachable; keep it routed correctly anyway. Also: filteredRows (tab filter strings "ready"/"unprocessed"/"ignored"/"linked"/"all"); handleIgnore, handleUnignore, handleUnlink, handleUnlinkRefund, handleRegenerateSuggestions, handleBulkIgnore, handleBulkImport (reads `statementRows` and `ruleVerdictFor` directly, so it is not a stable callback); drawer state creatingForRow / creatingRefundForRow / linkingForRow / ruleFormForRow with closeDrawer; a custom "…" overlay driven by menuAnchorPos/menuForRow; the toast; and a 3s AI poll that does `setStatement(cur => cur.map(_.copy(aiSuggestions = ...)))`. That creates a new aiSuggestions reference every tick, which is why case-class `==` matters for memo comparison.
  - The drawer renders BankRowCreateExpenseForm (Props: stmtId, row, merchants, categories, ruleList, aiSuggestion, ctx, onSuccess, onCancel, onNewEntities; prefill via `BankRowCreateExpenseForm.initialSelection(row, rules, merchants, categories, aiSuggestion)`, rule winner first, then AI), BankRowCreateRefundForm (stmtId, rowId, row, merchants, categories, ruleList, ctx, onSuccess, onCancel), BankRowLinkPicker and BankRowRuleForm, all in the same pages package.
  - Compat layer: web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/webapp/utils/slinkyUtils/compat/MuiCompat.scala (paginationProps, textFieldProps, autocompleteInputChange, tabValue), tested in web/src/test/.../compat/MuiCompatSpec.scala. Any new JS cast goes here, not in the page.
  - No existing usage in web of mui.Menu, mui.Tooltip, React.memo or useCallback. Existing hook examples: Hooks.useMemo in BankStatementAutoReconcilePage:81 and I18nHooks; Hooks.useRef in UserEditPage. mui.MenuItem is used as `mui.MenuItem.normal()(label).withKey(k).build` (ImportRulesPage).
  - Tests: web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPageSpec.scala (AnyWordSpec + must Matchers; pure-function tests for resultLabel, suggestionsPending, canRegenerateSuggestions, resolveImport, with helpers merchant/rule/done). Existing subjects like "BankStatementReviewPage.resultLabel" break the naming rule; don't rename them, but name new blocks by method only.

CONVENTIONS
- Frontend (docs/guide/frontend.md, antipatterns.md):
  - RULE-FE-001 component shape (case class Props, `val component = FunctionalComponent[Props]`, `def apply(...): KeyAddingStage`).
  - RULE-FE-002: object-level vals hold only plain JS/CSSPropertiesUtils, never ReactElement/KeyAddingStage. RULE-FE-003: `def` for elements reused in one render.
